title: Pre-Computing Embeddings
summary: Compute reusable document vectors ahead of requests using content identity, version lineage, and an explicit freshness strategy.
overview: Pre-computing embeddings moves document encoding out of the interactive retrieval path. Stable source chunks are embedded during ingestion or a scheduled backfill, then stored for repeated search. Query embeddings are usually still computed per request, though exact reusable queries may have their own cache. The approach improves latency only if precomputed vectors remain compatible and current.

A content-addressed design can avoid re-embedding unchanged chunks, but the cache key must include the embedding model, tokenizer or preprocessing contract, and relevant normalization settings. Identical text in two tenants may share computation only under an approved policy; their access metadata and retrieval identities still remain separate.

production.poc: A prototype compares request-time document encoding with an offline index build and records the resulting freshness delay.
production.production: Production hashes source chunks, versions embedding configurations, and retries failed records without restarting the whole corpus.
production.scale: Enterprise scale separates bulk backfills from incremental updates, estimates migration cost, and tracks source coverage and visibility before switching indexes.

components.name: Source manifest
components.role: Lists document revisions and the chunks expected in an embedding build.

components.name: Content hash cache
components.role: Reuses compatible vectors for unchanged approved content.

components.name: Embedding workers
components.role: Encode bounded batches with validated dimensions and normalization.

components.name: Vector artifact store
components.role: Persists vectors and lineage before or alongside index publication.

components.name: Coverage controller
components.role: Verifies that the expected source set is represented and current.

flow.title: Build a source snapshot
flow.description: Record the exact documents and revisions included in the build.

flow.title: Normalize and chunk
flow.description: Apply a versioned preprocessing policy with stable source offsets.

flow.title: Check reusable vectors
flow.description: Look up content hashes under the complete embedding configuration identity.

flow.title: Encode missing chunks
flow.description: Batch only required work and retain per-record failure status.

flow.title: Publish the index
flow.description: Write vectors with source and permission metadata, then verify search visibility.

flow.title: Maintain incrementally
flow.description: Process changed or deleted chunks and rebuild in parallel when the embedding space changes.

useCase.title: Preparing a policy archive for search
useCase.situation: A records service exposes decades of approved policy documents through an internal assistant.
useCase.problem: Encoding documents during queries makes response time unpredictable and repeats expensive work.
useCase.requirement: Prepare searchable vectors offline while keeping new policy revisions current.
useCase.architecture: A snapshot manifest drives a backfill, and content hashes reuse unchanged paragraphs across approved revisions.
runtime: The nightly update identifies changed chunks and encodes only those required.
Coverage checks confirm that every active document revision has searchable vectors before publication.
useCase.failure: If an embedding model changes, a new index is built separately rather than mixing new vectors with the old space.
useCase.impact: Measure build coverage, update lag, avoided encoding work, and query latency; precomputation transfers cost in time rather than eliminating it.

tradeoffs.cost: Requires precise configuration keys and access-aware identity.
Temporarily increase storage and compute cost.

failures.scenario: Stale vector reused after model change
failures.detection: Cache returns a vector with incompatible representation metadata.
failures.recovery: Include model and preprocessing identity in every cache key.

failures.detection: Published index coverage is below the source manifest.
failures.recovery: Track per-record status and block incomplete publication where required.

mistakes.fix: Include model, preprocessing, and normalization settings.

mistakes.mistake: Treating vector reuse as shared authorization
mistakes.fix: Keep tenant and source permissions separate.

mistakes.mistake: Recomputing the entire corpus for small edits
mistakes.fix: Use stable chunk hashes and incremental manifests.

whenToUse: Use for stable or slowly changing retrieval corpora.
Use when document encoding would dominate request latency.
Use for large index builds with repeated unchanged content.
whenNotToUse: Avoid stale precomputation for rapidly changing data without updates.
Do not mix incompatible embedding spaces.
Avoid cross-scope reuse without an approved data policy.
checklist: Plan incremental updates and parallel migrations.
